item: A release-run restore that failed reads error, not measured; a resume retakes it; the passphrase is kept out of what the restore child and a kept fresh install write
key_paths: src/monitoring/release_run.py; src/monitoring/release_run_fresh_restore.py; src/monitoring/secret_scrub.py; src/api/diagnostics/release_run.py; src/static/app-diagnostics.js; tests/test_release_run.py; tests/test_secret_scrub.py; docs/product/RELEASE_0.4_GATE.md
summary: From the 2026-09-30 diagnostics: two of the four release runs that reached the restore (instances 085218 and 085230, both run on 2026-09-26) had failed there, one refused by the restore engine's own staging check after 128 s and one dead after 53 minutes with Error creating function, and the report recorded both as measured with rows A and I over an empty restore block (row K read measured from the P0 trio, its scan of the restored corpus empty): the phase was measured whenever the parent returned, and neither the child's own ok nor its exit status was read. A restore now counts only when its child reported ok, its process exited 0 and its restore was committed; otherwise the phase reads error with the child's own words, rows A and I read error, rows E and K say the restored install's reading is not counted, and a resume retakes the restore and owes the passphrase as a first run does (the pre-migration restore included); a state file an earlier build wrote keeps no restore this rule would not count. The passphrase is taken out of what the child says where it writes its result and again where the parent records it, and out of the run journal and import reports a kept fresh install leaves on the drive (a file that cannot be rewritten is removed). Unit-proved only; no instance has run a release run on it, and the two failed runs are not evidence for row A. Lesson: LESSONS.md, the entry A PHASE'S STATUS WAS THE RUNNER'S, NOT THE CHILD'S.
